recommendation: Keep the commit. It completes the FHIR-16428 HTTP-page portion of the same CORS guidance family without duplicating or weakening the detailed security-page wording.
issue_request: FHIR-16428 was Published and resolved Persuasive. It asked that the HTTP page stop recommending CORS as a gross security recommendation because CORS is appropriate only under specific conditions and can be dangerous if configured permissively.
initial_application: Commits 6f65400358 and b294d647ed moved the ongoing CORS security-holes note to source/security.html and added a security-page reference from source/http.html, but current source/http.html still said servers SHOULD implement CORS and linked the CORS phrase to Enable-CORS rather than to the security guidance.
additional_context: FHIR-13827 later softened the security-page wording to say servers should consider CORS when browser-based JavaScript clients are desirable and should consult W3C, Enable-CORS, and Moesif guidance. Leaving the HTTP page as a blanket SHOULD contradicted that applied security-page decision.
reconciliation: Rewrote the source/http.html note so it no longer recommends that all servers implement CORS. It now says browser-based clients may require CORS support and points to security.html#http for CORS considerations and related security guidance.
source_changes: source/http.html: replaced the CORS SHOULD recommendation with a pointer to security.html#http for CORS considerations.

related_jiras.note: Later security WG CORS wording confirms the HTTP page should defer to conditional security guidance rather than make a blanket recommendation.
Moved the ongoing CORS security-holes note from http.html to security.html and explains nearby historical edits.

evidence_items.learned: This establishes the final WG intent for the HTTP page not to make a blanket CORS security recommendation.
